q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance suitor undesired) asserts as a kind-level generic that suitors are undesired, which the sentence never says: "undesired" restricts the object of the purpose clause, and asserting it of the kind at large is content the words do not put there.
The passive subject "PeopleSoft" is the active's direct object of "equip" but is given Recipient, a role the instruction set reserves for an indirect object / "to"-goal / addressee of communication.

The object of the "with"-PP is placed in the direct-object role Theme, though the instruction set puts a prepositional verb's object in the preposition-named oblique (its own example is "dealt with the appeal") and splits a with-phrase only into CoAgent / Instrument.

"known as a 'poison pill'" is flattened into (Member sk_defence_1 poison_pill), asserting the nickname as outright kind membership and dropping the participial post-modifier that the instruction set treats as a reduced relative.

q2_gaps: a "known as <quoted term>" nickname appositive: Name carries a string literal for proper nouns only, and the reduced-relative rule would force an odd "know" event, so a term-of-art label has no licensed form

a restrictive adjective on a bare/generic plural object ("thwart undesired suitors"): a bare class symbol admits no modifier, and the only alternative on offer (Inheritance on the kind) asserts a generic the text does not state
notes: The anti_takeover_defence fusion with its genus (and correctly no modifier genus, since "anti-takeover" is not a gradable/positional/material adjective), the agentless passive "designed" with Patient, the purpose head To, and leaving the idiom poison_pill undecomposed all follow the instruction set.
